units: Sot. 12ᵇ; Ex. R. s. 1 אמתה חד אמר ידה the word אמתה (Ex. II, 5)—one says it means אַמָּתָהּ, her arm, the other says it means אֲמָתָהּ, her maid-servant (v. אָמָה).—Lam. R. introd. (R. Josh. 2) א׳ דבצלי׳ an arm (direction-post) &c.; v. בְּצַל; Koh. R. to XII, 7 אם.—אַמַּת (בית) השחי the arm up to the axilla, arm-pit, name of an opening in a Temple door; v. however, infra. 4).

senses.gloss: cubit, a measure equal to the distance from the elbow to the tip of the middle-finger.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 5b:1">Keth. 5ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Menachot 11a:6">Men. 11ᵃ</cite> <he>זו א׳</he> this one (the middle-finger) is used for defining the cubit measure.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 17:10">Kel. XVII, 10</cite> <he>אַמַּת הבנין וכ׳</he> the standard cubit of the Temple proportions was six, that of the vessels five hand-breadths.
<cite ref="Shabbat 31a">Sabb. 31ᵃ</cite> <he>א׳ הבנין</he> the builder’s cubit (instrument).—<he>א׳ על א׳</he> square-cubit.

<cite ref="Zevachim 62b:16">Zeb. 62ᵇ</cite> (<cite ref="C01298"><he>גרומה</he></cite>) <he>א׳ גדומה</he>; <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 4:4:4">Y. Yoma IV, 41ᶜ</cite> bot. <he>גמודה</he> a reduced cubit; v. <cite ref="C00231"><he>גָּדַם</he></cite>; also called <he>א׳ בת ששה עצבות</he> a cubit of six hand-breadths pressed together (sorrowing), opp. to <he>א׳</he> (<he>בת ששה</he>) <he>שוחקות</he> a cubit of six wide-spread (laughing) hand-breadths.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shekalim 6:4:4">Y. Shek. VI, end, 50ᵇ</cite>.—
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 31:11">Gen. R. s. 31</cite> (<he>א׳</he>) <cite ref="V00045"><he>תביקין</he></cite> Theban (Egypt.) cubit(?).

<cite ref="Bava Batra 99b:4">B. Bath. 99ᵇ</cite> <he>אמה בית השלחין</he> land for digging a dyke of one cubit’s width; <he>א׳ בית הקילון</he> (Var. <cite ref="S01271"><he>קלון</he></cite>, <cite ref="O00658"><he>סילון</he></cite>) land for a creek or pond for watering cattle and washing clothes, of one cubit’s width.

Yoma V, 6 אלו ואלו מתערבין בא׳ the blood of both was mixed in the sewer; Tam. III, 6; B. Mets. 33ᵃ; Y. Hor. III, 48ᵇ top אמת (בית) השחי a sewer in the Temple called the duct of the arm-pit (from its shape; v. Grætz Monatsschr. 1880, p. 289; [emendation שית unnecessary]; v. supra.—Pl. אַמּוֹת cubits.
